body.statement: Under the finite-population Lindeberg condition and any deterministic sequence of known hit probabilities \(r_C\to r\), every subsequence contains a further subsequence and a \(\lambda\in\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\) for which \(\sqrt C(\widehat U_C-U_C)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma(r,\lambda))\). Along local welfare arrays, the empirical-best rule obeys \(\limsup_{C\to\infty}\sqrt C\,\mathbb E[\max_k U_{C,k}-U_{C,\delta_{\mathrm{EB}}(\widehat U_C)}]\le\kappa(K-1)\sqrt{H(r;f)}\), uniformly over fixed \(h\) in compact sets and compatible coupling subsequences. The expectation is finite for every \(C\) because \(\widehat U_C\) is total. Hence \(rStar\) and \(pStar\) minimize this certified worst-case Gaussian pairwise-regret bound within their respective design domains.
body.justification: This connects the certified allocation criterion to finite-population welfare loss using assignment randomness alone.
body.gap: LiDing2017 derives vector finite-population central limit theorems, and Joo2025 studies minimax regret for a fixed covariance; neither takes a supremum over the sharp coupling set while choosing the saturation design.
body.consumer: Investigators obtain an interpretable upper bound on the cluster count needed to keep worst-case policy-selection regret below a prespecified tolerance.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
E_C=\sqrt C(\widehat U_C-U_C),\qquad
h_C=\sqrt C(U_C-\mu_0\mathbf1_K).
\]
Theorem~\(\texttt{thm:sharp-covariance-set}\) gives, on a further subsequence, a \(\lambda\in\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\) for which the covariance of \(E_C\) tends to \(\Sigma(r,\lambda)\).  For fixed \(a\in\mathbb R^K\), \(a^{\mathsf T}E_C\) is a sum of independent centered cluster contributions.  The positive limiting hit rates bound inverse probabilities, and \(0\le W\le1\) bounds every unnormalized contribution.  Thus each normalized summand is \(O(C^{-1/2})\), so the Lindeberg remainder is eventually zero.  Taylor expansion of its characteristic function has a total third-order remainder \(O(C^{-1/2})\), and multiplication of the factors gives
\[
a^{\mathsf T}E_C\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(r,\lambda)a).
\]
This also holds at zero variance.  Applying the identity for every \(a\) proves by Cramér--Wold that
\[
E_C\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma(r,\lambda)).
\tag{8}
\]
This derives, rather than assumes, the limit law from independence, positivity, bounded outcomes, and the stated Lindeberg condition.

Assumption~\(\texttt{ass:local-welfare-array}\) gives \(h_C\to h\), and the empirical-best selector acts on \(h_C+E_C\).  Pass to a further subsequence on which the least maximizer \(i_C\) of \(h_C\) is constant, equal to \(i\).  Then \(i\) maximizes \(h\).  Put \(d_{ij}=h_i-h_j\ge0\).  If \(j\ne i\) is selected, then
\(h_{C,j}+E_{C,j}\ge h_{C,i}+E_{C,i}\).  The scaled loss is bounded by the range of \(h_C\), hence is uniformly bounded.  From (8), one-dimensional contrast convergence, and \(h_C\to h\),
\[
\limsup_C\sqrt C\,\mathbb E[
\max_kU_{C,k}-U_{C,\delta_{\mathrm{EB}}(\widehat U_C)}]
\le
\sum_{j\ne i}d_{ij}
\Phi\!\left(-\frac{d_{ij}}{\sqrt{V_{ij}(r,\lambda)}}\right),
\tag{9}
\]
where a term is zero if \(d_{ij}=0\) or \(V_{ij}=0\).  The zero-variance case follows because the limiting contrast is then the negative constant \(-d_{ij}\).

By the definition of \(\kappa\), each term in (9) is at most
\(\kappa\sqrt{V_{ij}(r,\lambda)}\), and every such variance is at most \(H(r;f)\).  Therefore
\[
\limsup_C\sqrt C\,\mathbb E[
\max_kU_{C,k}-U_{C,\delta_{\mathrm{EB}}(\widehat U_C)}]
\le\kappa(K-1)\sqrt{H(r;f)}.
\]
Uniformity over \(h\) in a compact set follows by contradiction: a violating sequence has a convergent \(h\)-subsequence and then, by finiteness of \(T\), a compatible-coupling subsequence to which the argument applies.  Finite-\(C\) regret is bounded by one because every \(U_{C,k}\in[0,1]\).  Finally, the definition of \(rStar,pStar\) and Theorem~\(\texttt{thm:robust-design-kkt}\) minimize \(H\) on the two domains, and the displayed bound is increasing in \(H\).
